sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William & Ade Tatak Paputungan. 2017. Notes from the field: Lolak: another moribund language of Indonesia, with supporting audio. Language Documentation & Conservation 11: 328-366. hdl 10125/24758.
sources.note: p. 334 §2.1 Stress: 'Similar to the other Mongondow-Gorontalo languages, stress is not contrastive in Lolak, in contrast to most of the core Central Philippine languages such as Tagalog, Cebuano, and Bikol. … stress in Lolak regularly falls on the word-final syllable, even in Indonesian loanwords where it would be expected to fall on the penultimate syllable instead.' Again subgroup-level for non-contrastiveness; placement stated for Lolak only; Kaidipang not named.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2016. Notes from the field: Ponosakan: the sounds of a silently dying language of Indonesia, with supporting audio. Language Documentation & Conservation 10: 394-423. hdl 10125/24700.
sources.note: p. 399: 'As in other Mongondow-Gorontalo languages, stress is not contrastive in Ponosakan, and regularly falls on word-final syllables, with a few unpredictable exceptions where it falls on the penultimate syllable, e.g., siˈene [siˈʔene] "who".' Subgroup-level remark (Ponosakan is Mongondow branch, Kaidipang is Gorontalic); Kaidipang not named; the final-stress placement is asserted for Ponosakan only.

sources.citation: Usup, H. Hunggu Tadjuddin; Hj. H. Alitu-Pakaja; Johny Loho; Rocky Posumah; Santje Iroth. 1999. Kamus Bahasa Indonesia-Kaidipang (A-K). Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa. xviii+525 pp. ISBN 979-459-972-7.
sources.note: Pendahuluan §7 'Informasi Singkat tentang Bahasa Kaidipang' (pp. xiv-xvii; PDF pp. 14-17) gives the segmental phoneme chart, phonotactics (all words vowel-final, syllable pattern -(K)V-(K)V, nasal clusters), a phonemic short/long vowel contrast (tala vs taalo), /d/~/r/ variation, two allophones of /l/, and moK- morphophonemics; it lists the earlier Kaidipang studies (Usup 1971, Usup et al. 1979, 1993, 1994). Nothing at all on stress/tekanan. fetched sources from the Wayback Machine capture (2024-04-16) of repositori.kemdikbud.go.id/23737/1/…; live repository unreachable.

sources.citation: Tangahu, Hindrawati & Alan Mustapa. 2025. Tingkat kekerabatan bahasa Kaidipang dan bahasa Gorontalo (kajian leksikostatistik). ALFABETA: Jurnal Bahasa, Sastra, dan Pembelajarannya 8(2): 289-306. doi:10.33503/alfabeta.v8i2.2090.
sources.note: Swadesh-list lexicostatistics only; no mention of tekanan/stress.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Mānoa. hdl 10125/101972.
sources.note: Kaidipang ('Bolang-Itang/Kaidipang', data from Lobel's own fieldwork in Kaidipang town) appears only in the pronoun chapter §4.3.2 (pp. 134-140); the only stress remarks concern Maranao and Bikol; nothing on Kaidipang stress.
